events.text: I am painting White step, green silence: an imagined snowy egret lifting a yellow foot above green water. Inspired by the NPS Presidio guide: https://www.nps.gov/prsf/learn/nature/snowy-egret.htm . Goal: long joined neck and body gestures, three feather values, and one compact brightest accent.
The broad ground has pale seams. Four wet bridges will join them before the bird, keeping a dark upper field and quieter light water.
Wet bridges joined the bands. I will place the egret slightly left of center with room for the bill and lifted foot. Cool shadow carries the body beneath a warmer upper plane.
The silhouette is continuous, but the crown is angular and the body still has a shadow hollow. I will fill the torso and widen the head before the small features.
Broad overlaps closed the hollow and rounded the head. The neck still has an elbow; I will establish the black bill and unequal legs so later corrections have firm proportions.
The lifted leg separates cleanly from the standing one. Warm feet and the small yellow eye patch will give the cool bird a restrained color focus.
The yellow accents stay small. The torso needs a readable folded wing: I will lay a cool lower plane and longer warm feathers, rather than outline every feather.
The feather passes changed relief more than value. I will test a wider, thinner cool wing plane with a stronger color separation, then judge it at both scales.
The thinner cool pass made a distinct lower wing, but its lower edge is a dark bar. A broad middle feather plane can soften that transition while extending two tail points.
Long tail feathers broke the blunt end, though their tips remain soft. The bird needs a place in the marsh: distant reeds will stay watery, with a low bank at the left.
The watery reeds almost disappear into the dry ground. I will retain that distant haze and add a few nearer, darker gestures on the opposite bank for depth.
The nearer reeds are visible but angular. I will anchor the standing foot with an interrupted ripple, leaving a gap beneath the raised foot so the step remains clear.
The ripple settles the standing foot. The neck still bends in straight facets; closely spaced curved points and broader paint should round the outer turn without thickening the whole neck.
The neck turn broadened but the head pass partly covered the eye. I will restore it once, then add two loose crest filaments beyond the silhouette.
The restored eye reads and two crest tips escape the edge. I will inspect the upper details before shaping the chest; the standard center close view clips the crown.
Upper review: the head is rounder than the neck bend. Keep the eye clear; develop the long chest plane below it.
Upper close-up confirms a clear eye and narrow bill; the neck retains a soft projecting elbow. I will develop chest feathers with unequal long tapers and keep the outer contour mostly intact.

Chest tapers remain mostly inside the original silhouette, changing surface direction more than shape. I will separate three overlapping wing groups with restrained cool gaps, then check for unwanted striping.
Fine wing marks are becoming stripes without much added volume. I will keep the broad wing groups and give the sparse lower-left space two low marsh leaves, quieter than the bird.
The new leaves are hollow crescents. I will fill their centers and tie them to the water with one short stem and a broken reflection.
Broad overlaps filled the leaves. I am beginning the refinement pass: a joined warm shoulder, quieter wing transition, and a narrow light along the standing leg should clarify the light direction.
The shoulder is joined; its broad light still competes with regular ridges. I will try one short brow accent alone and keep it only if it remains compact at whole view.
The brow accent remains short and warm. The feet are too faint beside the dark legs; three small yellow gestures will clarify the lifted toes and standing contact.
The feet read more clearly. Four broken low-contrast reflections will connect the bird to the water without duplicating its full silhouette.
The lower reflections widened into pale grey blocks instead of quiet fragments. I will cover their centers with matching green and retain only the interrupted outer edges.
Matching thin covers removed some pale color but enlarged the ridged patch. I will try loaded broad water paint once; if relief persists, keep that failed repair as evidence rather than chase it.

Loaded water covers increased regular relief instead of removing it. I will stop those repairs. Four final long feather planes will restore a coherent torso direction; the broad water patches remain a documented failed experiment.

Final review at 96 completed marks: joined neck and body, cool lower wing, warmer shoulder, clear eye, compact brow light and lifted yellow foot. Broad overlaps filled hollow leaves. Thin cool paint separated values, but narrow feather marks mostly changed relief. Water reflection covers widened ridged patches; neck elbow, soft tips, angular reeds and regular ridges remain. Stop here: more covers are unlikely to help. Human ratings remain unset.

creation.method: AI agent painted in local Atelier browser simulator in animated 1–4-stroke batches, choosing each next batch after actual whole/close screenshot inspections. No image generation or renderer changes.
creation.practiceGoal: Join long neck and body gestures, separate three feather values, and keep one compact brightest accent.

inspiration.description: An original imagined snowy egret lifting a yellow foot above green marsh water, sparked by the NPS guide; no copied finished composition.

creation.inspectionEvidence: Settled whole and 2.0x close screenshot pairs inspected at 25 distinct boundaries, plus repeated final pair and upper camera at 56. Initial camera assertion rejected active+pressed state; corrected. Focus timeout at 8 and misframed pair repeated with 1280x1400 viewport. At 56, corrected screenshot crop from viewport coordinates to page coordinates including scroll offset. Close zoom at 96 had not settled; repeated final pair before stopping. A captured count in the screenshot helper reused 004 filenames and overwrote intermediate files; those inspections were seen live but are not retained individually. Retained final pair copied to accurate 096 filenames, and corrected upper image retained. Actual exported PNG visually inspected.
creation.notes: All 28 text notes and camera events were recorded live; 89 total moments. JSON exported through browser before adding this retrospective creation metadata.
creation.stopReason: After deliberate 72–96 refinement and repeated final review, further fine feather passes changed relief more than volume, and water covers enlarged patches. Stopped without padding to 112.
